title: The Backward Becoming
tagline: A novel that opens at the far end of a life and turns back toward its beginning.
statusNote: Not yet published. Early chapters are with a small private circle of advance readers.
description: In the spring of 1972, an American nurse named Nell Hale is working in a cholera-relief camp outside Dacca. The novel opens there, at the far end of a life, on an afternoon that does not go the way the day was supposed to go.

Then it turns back to Calder, Kentucky — to a chicken pie carried into a front room in 1946, to a tenth birthday the January after, to a July afternoon at the river in 1951 — and works forward through the ordinary days that made her.

The Backward Becoming is a book about what a person is assembled from: a kitchen, a sandbar, the exact way a fork goes around the edge of a crust, and how much of a life turns out to have been decided on afternoons nobody thought to write down.
